# Context

This script provides select code to count Medicare and Medicaid behavioral health emergency department (ED) visits. Behavioral health ED visits have a primary diagnosis code for substance use disorder, severe mental illness, or mild-to-moderate mental health diagnoses (as defined in scripts `select_code_to_identify_MH_conditions.Rmd` and `select_code_to_identify_SUD.Rmd`).

We identify ED visits as described in [Handel et al. 2008](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17996983/) as any claim where:  
  
- The claim contains a CPT code for ED visit (CPT 99281-99285) or advanced life support (CPT 99288)    
- The claim contains an ED Revenue code (450-459 or 981) and is not paired with a laboratory only CPT   

To identify ED visits, this code assumes the user has created a combined claims table of Medicare encounters (from the Inpatient, Outpatient, and Carrier files) and TAF claims (from the Inpatient and Other Services file). 

Prior to combining claim sets, users should also exclude TAF crossover claims (crossover_clm_ind == 1) as well as Medicare encounters with procedure code modifiers that indicate a "Medicaid level of care" and were thus not paid for by Medicare, including U1-U9, UA, UB, UC, and UD. See [here](https://www.hcpcsdata.com/Modifiers/U)  

We used claim line dates to identify ED visits. When combining claim sets, users should combine the line_from_dt and line_thru_dt values on Medicare professional encounters with rev_cntr_from_dt and rev_cntr_thru_dt values on Medicare facility encounters, respectively, effectively creating a single line from and a single line thru date. 

Once claim sets are combined, the claims table (named "claims" below) should include the following columns:  
- bene_id  
- claim_id  
- from_dt (claim header begin date)    
- thru_dt (claim header end date)  
- line_from_dt (either the line date or revenue center from date)
- line_thru_dt (either the line date or revenue center thru date)
- primary diagnosis code  
- revenue center code  
- procedure code (cpt/hcpcs codes)  
- ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate (from the TAF Other Services file)
- source file ("taf" or "ma") 
- file type ("ma_op", "ma_ip", "ma_car", "taf_ot", "taf_ip")


# Load behavioral health code lookup tables

```{r}
# mental health icd codes
mh_codes <- fread("mental_health_icd_codes.csv")

# sud icd codes
load("ccw30_sud_codes.RData")

# behavioral health outpatient cpt codes
bh_cpts <- fread("outpt_bh_cpts.csv")
```


# Define ED codes

```{r}
# set codes as described in Handel et al.
cpt_handel <- as.character(99281:99285, 99288)
rev_handel <- str_pad(c(450:459, 981), width = 4, side = "left", pad = "0")
cpt_lab_handel <- c("G0001", 36400:36415, 43200:43272, 45300:45387, 70010:79999, 80048:89399, 93000:93278)
```


# Flag and restrict to ED claims

```{r}
# flag if claim line has ED revenue or CPT
claims[, `:=` (ed_cpt = hcpcs_cd %in% cpt_handel | ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate %in% cpt_handel,
               ed_lab_only = rev_cntr %in% rev_handel & (hcpcs_cd %in% cpt_lab_handel | 
                                                            ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate %in% cpt_lab_handel),
               ed_rev = rev_cntr %in% rev_handel)]

# flag ED
claims[ , ed :=  ed_cpt == T | (ed_rev == T & ed_lab_only == F)]

# keep only ED claims 
ed_claims <- claims[ed == T]
```


# Flag and restrict to behavioral health visits

```{r}
# flag each BH condition catgegory
ed_claims[ , `:=` (sud_dx  = icd_dgns_cd1 %in% sud_icd10,
                   mmmi_dx = icd_dgns_cd1 %in% mh_codes[condition == "mild_mod_mh", icd10],
                   smi_dx  = icd_dgns_cd1 %in% mh_codes[condition == "smi", icd10])] %>%
  .[ , bh_dx := mmmi_dx == T | sud_dx == T | smi_dx == T]

# keep only BH claims 
ed_claims <- ed_claims[bh_dx == T]
```


# Identify ED visit dates

Here we replace the claim header dates with line dates when available. Note: For MA encounters, revenue center dates and line dates were combined into one variable (line_from_dt and line_thru_dt) prior to combining MA and TAF claims.

```{r}
# replace the claim header date with the line/revenue center date when available
ed_claims[ , `:=` (from_dt = as.Date(ifelse(!is.na(line_from_dt), line_from_dt, from_dt)),
                   thru_dt = as.Date(ifelse(!is.na(line_thru_dt), line_thru_dt, thru_dt)))]
```


# Transform data to one day per row

```{r}
# flag one day claims
ed_claims[ , days := as.numeric(thru_dt - from_dt + 1)] %>% .[ , oneday := days == 1]

# separate one day and multi-day claims
ed_multiday <- ed_claims[oneday == F] %>% .[ , rownum := seq_along(1:.N)]
ed_oneday <- ed_claims[oneday == T]

# expand long so each day is on a separate row
ed_multiday_expand <- ed_multiday[, .(date = seq(from_dt, thru_dt, by = "day")), by = rownum]

# add back other vars
ed_multiday_expand <- merge(ed_multiday_expand, 
                            ed_multiday[ , c("from_dt", "thru_dt") := NULL],
                            by = "rownum", all = T)

# set from_dt and thru_dt equal to date
ed_multiday_expand[, `:=`(from_dt = date, thru_dt = date)] %>%
  .[, c("date", "rownum") := NULL]

# rejoin one-day and multi-day claims,  nrow should grow. 
nrow(ed_claims)
ed_claims <- rbind(ed_oneday, ed_multiday_expand)
nrow(ed_claims)

#drop vars
ed_claims[ , c("days", "oneday") := NULL]
rm(ed_oneday, ed_multiday, ed_multiday_expand)
```


# Drop more crossover claims from TAF

Some TAF claims have the same date of service, primary diagnosis code, and procedure code as a MA encounter. We consider these "crossover claims" that weren't flagged by crossover_clm_ind == 1. We exclude these from the dataset and attribute these services to MA.  

Before checking to see if MA and TAF claims match by procedure code, we need to clean up the TAF OT procedure code, since it can be in one of two different fields (hcpcs_cd or ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate). We'll create a unified procedure code variable that pulls the ED CPT from whichever field has it. 

```{r}
# if the ED CPT code is in the ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate field, move that value into hcpcs_cd
ed_claims[ed_cpt == T & !hcpcs_cd %in% cpt_handel, hcpcs_cd := ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate]

ed_claims$ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate <- NULL
```

```{r}
# separate MA and TAF
ed_all_ma  <- ed_claims[source == "ma"]
ed_all_taf <- ed_claims[source == "taf"] 

# merge MA onto TAF by date, diagnosis, and CPT
ed_all_taf <- merge(ed_all_taf,
                    unique(ed_all_ma[!is.na(hcpcs_cd), .(bene_id, from_dt, thru_dt, 
                                                         icd_dgns_cd1, hcpcs_cd, crossover_cpt = T)]),
                    by = c("bene_id", "from_dt", "thru_dt", "icd_dgns_cd1", "hcpcs_cd"), 
                    all.x = T) %>%
  .[is.na(crossover_cpt) , crossover_cpt := F]

# merge MA onto TAF by date, diagnosis, and Rev code
ed_all_taf <- merge(ed_all_taf,
                    unique(ed_all_ma[!is.na(rev_cntr), .(bene_id, from_dt, thru_dt, 
                                                         icd_dgns_cd1, rev_cntr, crossover_rev = T)]),
                    by = c("bene_id", "from_dt", "thru_dt", "icd_dgns_cd1", "rev_cntr"), 
                    all.x = T) %>%
  .[is.na(crossover_rev) , crossover_rev := F]



# create overall flag - true if: rev is crossover and cpt is crossover or missing, OR
#                                cpt is crossover and rev is crossover or missing
# (necessary because some days have both rev and CPT)
ed_all_taf[ , crossover := (crossover_rev == T & (crossover_cpt == T | is.na(hcpcs_cd))) |
                           (crossover_cpt == T & (crossover_rev == T | is.na(rev_cntr)))] %>%
  .[ , c("crossover_rev", "crossover_cpt") := NULL]

# bind TAF and MA back together
ed_claims <- rbind(ed_all_taf, ed_all_ma[ , crossover := F])

# drop crossover claims
ed_claims <- ed_claims[crossover == F]
```


# Roll up days to visits

Here we group together contiguous days, regardless of payer, so we can count distinct visits.

```{r}
# order data
ed_claims <- ed_claims[order(bene_id, from_dt, thru_dt)]

# group contiguous days
ed_claims[ , visit_id := chse::overlapping(from_dt, 
                                           thru_dt, 
                                           maxgap = 0), by = .(bene_id)]

# roll up values by visit
ed_claims[ , `:=` (start_dt = min(from_dt), 
                   end_dt = max(thru_dt), 
                   smi_dx = max(smi_dx), 
                   mmmi_dx = max(mmmi_dx), 
                   sud_dx = max(sud_dx),
                   taf = max(source == "taf"), 
                   ma = max(source == "ma")), by = .(bene_id, visit_id)] %>%
  .[ , days := as.numeric(end_dt - start_dt + 1)] 
```


# Assign diagnosis category

We assign diagnosis category hierarchically and count the visit as SUD if any visit claims were flagged as SUD, then SMI if any SMI, then mild to moderate mental health.  

```{r}
ed_claims[ , dx_cat := fcase(sud_dx  == T, "sud",
                             smi_dx  == T, "smi",
                             mmmi_dx == T, "mmmi")]
```


# Make unique

Make claims unique by visit date, diagnosis category, and payer

```{r}
ed_visits <- unique(ed_claims[ , .(bene_id, start_dt, dx_cat, ma, taf)])
```


# Limit to bene months observed

Keep only ed visits with a start date during which the enrollee was observed in the study cohort. In this chunk, "mbsf" is a table of enrollees in the analytic study sample at the enrollee-month level.

```{r}
ed_visits[, bene_mo := paste(bene_id, month(start_dt), year(start_dt), sep = "_")]
ed_visits <- merge(ed_visits, mbsf[ , .(bene_mo)], by = "bene_mo", all = F)
```


# Categorize payer

```{r}
# recreate source/payer variable
ed_visits[ , source := fcase(taf == 1 & ma == 1, "tafma",
                             taf == 1, "taf", 
                             ma  == 1, "ma")]
```


# Sum visits by year

Sum visits by diagnosis category and payer

```{r}
# create year variable
ed_visits[ , year := year(start_dt)]

# sum visits by setting and diagnosis
ed_visits <- ed_visits[ , .(n = uniqueN(start_dt)), by = .(bene_id, year, source, dx_cat)]

# create a column name combining source and dx_cat
ed_visits[ , varname := paste("ed", dx_cat, source, "n", sep = "_")]

# reshape to wide format
ed_visits <- dcast(ed_visits, bene_id + year ~ varname, value.var = "n", fill = 0) 

# set missing values to 0
outcome_vars <- names(ed_visits)[grepl("_taf|_ma", names(ed_visits))]
ed_visits[, (outcome_vars) := lapply(.SD, function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x)), .SDcols = outcome_vars]
ed_visits[, lapply(.SD, max), .SDcols = outcome_vars]
```
